faq.a: Veli is associated with the Arabic form وَلِي, whose core sense is veli; guardian, friend (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Veli?
faq.a: Veli is associated with Arabic. Veli is the Turkish form of Arabic وَلِيّ (Walī), meaning 'guardian, friend'.
Yes — the underlying form وَلِي is Arabic.
Veli can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Veli should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root و ل ي is Quranic, but Walī is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Veli, veli. Script forms are ولي, ولی, وَلِي, वली.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
